action_criteria.expected_evidence: MoCA 23/30 with every lost point in delayed recall (0/5 free, 2/5 multiple choice) and orientation; other sections full; apathy
action_criteria.label: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Severe anterograde amnesia with recognition at the 2nd percentile, executive function, language and reasoning average
action_criteria.label: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
action_criteria.rationale: The screen cannot separate a storage from a retrieval deficit; formal memory testing with recognition characterises the amnesia and documents a baseline for her fitness to practise.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Reversible causes negative (TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV); LDL 102 mg/dL on atorvastatin 20 mg
action_criteria.label: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, HbA1c, lipid panel)
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes reversible and nutritional contributors to an amnestic syndrome and characterises the lipid risk after an infarct.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Chronic left anterior and paramedian thalamic infarct (about 0.4 mL) in the region of the mamillothalamic tract, Fazekas 1, MTA 0
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
action_criteria.rationale: An abrupt amnestic syndrome with a normal acute CT: MRI shows small thalamic infarcts that CT misses and grades the medial temporal lobes.

action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG after the newly identified ischaemic infarct
action_criteria.rationale: Every ischaemic stroke gets an ECG; she was never worked up for stroke at the admission.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No vertebrobasilar, posterior cerebral or carotid stenosis or dissection
action_criteria.label: Obtain MR angiography of the head and neck for intracranial large-artery stenosis or dissection
action_criteria.rationale: Defensible to exclude a posterior-circulation stenosis behind a thalamic infarct; optional because a small perforator infarct is the usual cause.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal LV and LA, LVEF 62%, no thrombus or shunt
action_criteria.label: Obtain a transthoracic echocardiogram to look for a structural cardioembolic source
action_criteria.rationale: Reasonable after ischaemic stroke; optional because a small thalamic perforator infarct rarely has a cardiac source.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm throughout a 14-day recording, no atrial fibrillation
action_criteria.label: Order prolonged ambulatory rhythm monitoring for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
action_criteria.rationale: Defensible after a stroke that was never worked up; optional because the lesion is lacunar rather than cryptogenic.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not accept a normal head CT as excluding a strategic thalamic infarct
Do not diagnose a degenerative dementia when the deficit began on a datable day and has not progressed in eight months
Do not rely on the patient's own account of her function when apathy and amnesia are both present
Do not conclude 'mild cognitive impairment' from the screen total when one domain accounts for the loss and she cannot work
Do not start anticoagulation without a documented cardioembolic source
required_recommendations: Continue single antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 100 mg) for secondary prevention after the thalamic infarct [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary]
Lower blood pressure (144/84 mmHg) gradually to below 130/80 mmHg, checking orthostatic BP at each change [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary]
Increase atorvastatin from 20 mg to high-intensity dosing (LDL 102 mg/dL) [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary]
Address fitness to practise as a notary and driving with her and her husband, since the apathy prevents her from raising either
Arrange memory rehabilitation with external aids (diary, alarms, supervised appointments) and caregiver support

avoided_actions.rationale: A continuous, stable deficit since one dated day, with no episodic or stereotyped attacks: EEG has no diagnostic role.
No parkinsonism, fluctuations, hallucinations or dream enactment; a dopamine transporter scan does not address the question.
No feature of Lewy body disease or autonomic failure; cardiac sympathetic imaging does not inform this diagnosis.
An abrupt-onset stable deficit, not a subacute progressive multidomain syndrome: an untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune battery has no indication.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.

accepted: Vascular dementia: strategic single-infarct type, left anterior and paramedian thalamic infarct interrupting the mamillothalamic tract
major neurocognitive disorder due to vascular disease

differential.key_features: The onset was abrupt on a documented day and the deficit has been stable for eight months rather than progressive; the hippocampi are normal at Scheltens 0 and executive function and language are above average
The deficit is continuous rather than episodic, there are no stereotyped attacks, and the thalamic infarct explains it

No alcohol misuse (two glasses of wine weekly), no nutritional deficiency, no ophthalmoparesis or ataxia, and the lesion is unilateral thalamic rather than in the mamillary bodies and periaqueductal grey
Fazekas 1 change and a normal executive profile exclude the diffuse subcortical mechanism; the deficit is focal
Recognition memory is impaired at the 2nd percentile with an anatomically coherent lesion; the pattern is not inconsistent or effort-dependent

key_clinical_evidence: A small lesion in a strategic location produces a dementia out of proportion to its volume: about 0.4 mL in the anterior thalamus interrupts the mamillothalamic tract and with it the Papez circuit

Impaired recognition places the deficit at storage rather than retrieval, and storage-type amnesia localises to the hippocampal-diencephalic circuit — the opposite of the retrieval pattern of small-vessel disease
The screening total is a poor instrument for focal deficits: normal attention, executive function and language with a floor-level recall is a localising pattern, not mild impairment
CT misses small thalamic infarcts routinely, and a normal CT during the index admission is what allowed eight months to pass without a diagnosis

Apathy in a thalamic infarct is part of the lesion syndrome and it removes the patient's own capacity to report the deficit, which makes the informant history and the occupational assessment obligatory

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The loss falls on delayed recall, at floor even on multiple choice, and on orientation, while every other domain is normal; a focal profile at this severity with lost occupational function is a dementia
red_herrings.data_point: A MoCA of 23/30, in the mild range
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests mild cognitive impairment not amounting to dementia, and defers the workup

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Small thalamic infarcts are routinely invisible on CT; the MRI shows the chronic lesion that dates to that admission
red_herrings.data_point: A normal head CT during the index admission
red_herrings.intended_effect: Excludes a stroke and supports the discharge diagnosis of a transient confusional state

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Single unambiguous strategic lesion with a textbook amnestic profile; the difficulty is only in not being reassured by a MoCA of 23 and a normal CT
key_educational_points: A strategic infarct produces a deficit out of proportion to lesion volume; anterior thalamus, genu of the internal capsule, caudate and angular gyrus are the classic sites
Recognition memory testing separates storage from retrieval deficits and thereby localises the lesion
A normal CT does not exclude a small thalamic infarct
Screening totals conceal focal profiles; the per-domain breakdown is what carries the information

patient.history_present_illness: Dr. Elena Marchetti is a 68-year-old notary who was admitted eight months ago with sudden confusion and drowsiness that developed over an hour while she was at her desk. She was hospitalised for four days, a CT of the head was reported as normal, and she was discharged on aspirin with a diagnosis of a transient confusional state. Her husband reports that she has never returned to her previous self. She is alert, articulate and socially appropriate — colleagues who meet her briefly notice nothing — but she cannot retain new information at all: she asks the same question repeatedly within the hour, cannot remember whether she has eaten, and has twice arranged two appointments for the same time. She has not been able to return to notarial work, where retention of case detail is essential. Strikingly, she is not distressed by any of this and does not spontaneously mention it; the account comes entirely from her husband. There has been no further abrupt event, no headache, no weakness, no visual symptoms, no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. Her blood pressure has been in the 140-150 range. Her decline is not progressive: the deficit appeared on one day and has been stable since.

neurological_exam.additional: Marked apathy with preserved social comportment. No frontal release signs. Pulse regular at 70.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full without vertical gaze restriction. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech fluent and articulate.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal base, stride and arm swing. Tandem gait intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, articulate and socially appropriate; oriented to person, place, month and year, but gives the wrong date and day of the week. Conversation coherent and fluent. Confabulates mildly when asked about the previous day. Striking apathy and lack of concern about her situation. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk, tone and strength throughout. No drift, no tremor.
